subject: vc3 kill ROOT CAUSE = jetsam per-process limit (ns1 code7); fix + payload restaged (vcodecd bf89b8e2, selftest 702980f0)
body: Verified from xnu headers: 'reason ns 1 code 0x7' = OS_REASON_JETSAM / JETSAM_REASON_MEMORY_PERPROCESSLIMIT (not a fault: no SIGBUS issue; the core bridge already handles SIGSEGV+SIGBUS). Both kills symbolize to map_locked <- n2a32_mem_alloc <- n2elf_load (memset zero-fill while loading the first vendor library, about 2 MB into its span). The host's peak RSS for the whole vendor run is 21 MB (14.5 MB now), so the limit the kernel applied must have been tiny: the launchd JetsamMemoryLimit 1024 evidently did not apply (inferred). vc4 (20:20) ran the OLD binaries, same offsets. FIX: (1) include/n2memlimit.h: vcodecd and n2vcd_selftest call memorystatus_control(SET_MEMLIMIT_PROPERTIES, self, 3072 MB fatal) at startup (root is enough per kern_memorystatus.c) and log before/after/errno plus phys_footprint; (2) emu/n2a32_mem.c no longer memsets never-touched guest pages (PG_DIRTY bit), so nothing is pre-touched; (3) n2a32_mem_set_log() hook: mprotect failures with errno, big maps, and every mprotect at level 3; (4) selftest: a T0 jetsam line, a 'mem <step> footprint= rss=' line at each step, a crash handler for SIGSEGV/BUS/ILL/FPE on an alternate stack logging sig/si_code/si_addr, and T4 logs sig/si_code/host address via the new n2a32_last_fault(); (5) guest-vcodec.sh JetsamMemoryLimit 1024 -> 3072 (coordinator-authorized). Tests green native + N2A32_MEM_GRANULE=16384: V02 868/866, V10-V20, IV 80, V03, V30-V34, IP 854, DEC05 1150, T01. Built: ios/build.sh /tmp/n2hw-opus-lead/out (vcodecd bf89b8e25e6f8b4e, n2vcd_selftest 702980f0f6f6f59f, n2vcd_probe 74b9da43ef769d89 = the q10ja probe source); staged with the exact step-2a command -> payload-vcodec; rehearse-vcodec.sh REHEARSAL_OK. On the next run look for 'T0 jetsam raised' / 'N2VCD jetsam raised'; if it says NOT raised with an errno, the limit must come from launchd/jetsamproperties.
